content:
hector: Heads up — after the infra terraform bump I'm seeing intermittent 502s from the inference gateway. NLB reports unhealthy targets, but pods are fine. Anyone seen NLB healthcheck / k8s service port weirdness?
emma: Which service/namespace? nlb -> target group uses the Service's port mapping for health checks usually.
hector: namespace: inference-prod, svc: inference-gateway-svc. Quick snippet of the service we applied:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-gateway-svc
  namespace: inference-prod
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port: "traffic-port"
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    app: inference-gateway
  ports:
    - name: grpc
      port: 8500
      targetPort: grpc
      nodePort: 30900
```
hector: note targetPort is a named port (`grpc`) and container exposes 8500, but the containerPort in pod spec is 8500 (no named container port).
ajay: Named targetPort requires the container port to have the same name in pod spec. If k8s can't resolve the name it falls back? That can make NLB healthchecks hit the wrong port.
maria: Also watch externalTrafficPolicy: Local vs Cluster. With Local, NodePort traffic only forwarded to local pods and healthchecks to nodes can show unhealthy if no pod on that node. Which externalTrafficPolicy are we using?
hector: We left externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster (default) in this svc.
emma: Ok — two likely problems: 1) targetPort name not present on container (so resolves to 0 or wrong), 2) NLB healthcheck port annotation 'traffic-port' is fine but if port mapping is wrong TG will fail. Quick repro: run `kubectl get endpoints -n inference-prod inference-gateway-svc -o yaml` and check endpoint port numbers.
ajay: Quick fixes: either change targetPort to numeric 8500, or add name: grpc to containerPort in the pod spec. Example patch:```yaml
containers:
- name: gateway
  image: redwood/inference-gateway:stable
  ports:
  - containerPort: 8500
    name: grpc
```
maria: Alternatively, set the healthcheck to a specific port via annotation (e.g., '8500') while we roll that fix, but I'd prefer fixing the port naming in the pod so service semantics are explicit.
infra-bot: infra-bot: detected 3 failed target healthchecks on TG arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:.../tg-0a1b2c — health check reason: Target.Skipped — port conflict detected.
hector: Thanks — I'll open a tiny k8s manifest PR to add the container port name and switch targetPort to numeric in the svc as safety. I'll ping codeowners and run a canary. ETA ~30m.
emma: When you open PR include `kubectl get endpoints` output and the current svc yaml so reviewer can validate endpoints update.
ajay: Also add a note in terraform changelog: avoid changing svc port names without coordinating Pod/container changes. We had a drift where terraform updated svc before deployment.
hector: good call — will add a rollback plan: change svc -> patch pods -> monitor TG then roll forward.
maria: If you want a fast test, patch the svc in-cluster first (kubectl apply) in a canary namespace to verify NLB health.
hector: will do. pinging @emma and @ajay in the PR once ready :thumbsup:
emma: :+1:
infra-bot: infra-bot: scheduled health re-check in 5m for TG arn:...
hector: closing loop later with postmortem if anything unexpected shows up."
